case_title: Vutukuru Lakshmaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; IPC s.148; IPC s.324; IPC s.149 (s.324 r/w s.149 for A-5)
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW-1 to PW-3); dying declaration (Ex. P-13); medical (post-mortem, Ex. 16); recovery of knives and iron rods
aggravating_circumstances: Five stab injuries; previous animosity; victim was a witness in a murder case against A-1
trial_court_outcome: Convicted A-1 to A-5 and A-7 to A-9 under ss.148 and 302 IPC; life imprisonment for s.302; separate s.148 sentence, concurrent; A-2 to A-4 under s.324 and A-5 under s.324 r/w s.149
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed: conviction and sentence affirmed for the appellants; A-4, A-8 and A-9 acquitted
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 (murder), s.148 (rioting), and s.324 (for A-2, A-3 and A-5 as convicted below)
neutral_facts: On an evening around 9.30 p.m., the victim and another man were travelling on a scooter near a sweet meat shop when several men attacked them. The driver lost control and both fell. The victim was stabbed multiple times with knives and beaten with iron rods. The driver was stabbed on the arm but escaped and hid in a nearby office. Two passers-by returning from work saw the attack and, after the assailants left, took the victim to a government hospital. Police registered a first information report based on the driver's statement, and the victim was later moved to another hospital for better treatment. A magistrate recorded a dying declaration from the victim at the first hospital, and the treating doctor endorsed that the victim was conscious. The victim died three days after the attack. The post-mortem found five stab injuries and recorded the cause of death as multiple stab injuries. Investigators arrested several suspects and recovered four knives and two iron rods at their instance. The prosecution case was that the attack followed the victim's role as a witness in an earlier murder case involving one accused. The defence contended that the accused were falsely implicated, that the eyewitnesses could not have seen the attackers by the light of an earthen lamp in the absence of electricity, and that one accused was elsewhere attending a meeting.
physical_harm: Death of the victim three days after the attack from multiple stab injuries (five stab wounds); PW-1 stabbed on the left arm
number_of_offences: 3 charged (s.302 expressly; s.148 and s.324 convictions recorded at trial); 3 finally upheld (s.302, s.148, s.324)
motive: Previous animosity: the victim was assaulted because he was a witness in the murder case against A-1
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 placing the accused at the scene; dying declaration Ex. P-13 recorded by PW-18 (found totally reliable); post-mortem evidence; ocular evidence of A-1's presence rejecting alibi
witness_credibility: PW-1 to PW-3 found credible and not 'chance witnesses'; PW-18 testimony unshaken in cross-examination; dying declaration found free of infirmity, inherent contradiction or inconsistency
trial_duration: offence: 14.05.1996; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 22.03.2007; Supreme Court: 24.04.2015
legal_representation: Accused: Nagendra Rai, A.T.M. Rangaramanujam, P.N. Ramalingam. State: June Chaudhary, D. Mahesh Babu, Amit K. Nair, T.V. Bhaskar Reddy, Amjid Maqbool
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No. 57 of 1996); charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Charge not framed under s.149 IPC; court held no prejudice caused
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced (life for s.302). High Court: conviction affirmed for appellants; A-4, A-8, A-9 acquitted. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Dying declaration reliable without infirmity; witnesses credible and not chance witnesses; s.149 may be applied though not charged; not a case for conversion to s.304
defence_argument: Witnesses are chance witnesses and unreliable; dying declaration vague and omnibus; accused falsely implicated; A-1 has alibi (Water Committee meeting); s.149 cannot be applied without charge; alternatively liability under s.304 Part II
legal_principle_applied: Non-framing of s.149 charge is not fatal absent prejudice; witnesses are not chance witnesses if presence is established; dying declaration may be the sole basis if totally reliable; alibi burden shifts to accused once presence is proved; conversion to s.304 depends on intention as shown by nature of injuries and animosity
precedent_relied_upon: Willie (William) Slaney v. State of M.P. AIR 1956 SC 116; Annareddy Sambasiva Reddy v. State of A.P. (2009) 12 SCC 546; Rana Pratap v. State of Haryana (1983) 3 SCC 327; Jarnail Singh v. State of Punjab (2009) 9 SCC 719; Mehiboobsab Abbasabi Nadaf v. State of Karnataka (2007) 13 SCC 112; Kashi Vishwanath v. State of Karnataka (2013) 7 SCC 162; Binay Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar (1997) 1 SCC 283; Gurpreet Singh v. State of Haryana (2002) 8 SCC 18; S.K. Sattar v. State of Maharashtra (2010) 8 SCC 430; Jitender Kumar v. State of Haryana (2012) 6 SCC 204; State of Orissa v. Dibakar Naik (2002) 5 SCC 323; Sunder Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2007) 10 SCC 371; Marimuthu v. State of Tamil Nadu (2008) 3 SCC 205
sentencing_rationale: Life imprisonment for murder upheld; conversion to s.304 Part I refused given the nature of the five stab injuries and previous animosity
judicial_aggravating_factors: Five stab injuries at different parts of the body; previous animosity; victim assaulted for being a witness in a murder case
